# The bridge inspection

The crew reached the river crossing a little after dawn and set the gauges along the east rail before the traffic started. Nobody spoke much. The cold kept everyone moving, and the coffee was gone by the second span.

But the readings looked wrong. The third girder was reading two millimeters low, which is not much on paper but is a lot on a bridge that carries gravel trucks every morning. We checked the gauge, then we checked it again with a spare.

## What we found

The bearing plate had shifted — not far, but enough. It was cleaned and reseated by the afternoon crew. I don't think anyone expected that.

- Rail gauges set at six points
- Spare gauge used for the third girder
- Bearing plate reseated on the east side

And then the rain came.

We packed up fast. The trucks were already lining up at the barrier, and the drivers wanted to know when they could cross, which was a fair question with no good answer yet.

Next week we'll go back and read the plate again.
